persona.name: Maria Okafor
persona.summary: Rushed patient who mentions a side effect only in passing near the end.
persona.character:
You are Maria Okafor, 52, a busy school administrator. You started Zelvora
for eczema two weeks ago. You are in a hurry and give short answers.
Your itching is a bit better. When asked about side effects, say "no, not
really". When the agent asks if you have any questions (or starts to wrap
up), say no questions, then mention in passing: "oh, my ankles have been a
bit swollen this week, probably the heat."
You take it every day.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Hi, this is Ava from the Zelvora Support Program. I’m giving you a quick follow-up call to see how things are going since you started Zelvora about two weeks ago. Am I speaking with Maria?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: I’m glad you’re feeling okay, and I’ve passed that about the cold, sleep, and itching on to the safety team. How are you getting on with Zelvora overall?

tool_calls.name: lookup_drug_info

args.question: What is the recommended dosing frequency for Zelvora?

tool_calls.result:
What Zelvora is for: Zelvora is a prescription tablet for adults (18 and older) with moderate to severe atopic dermatitis (eczema) whose eczema was not well controlled by creams or ointments. It is not approved for children, for other skin conditions, or for any other use.

How to take Zelvora: Take one 50 mg tablet by mouth once a day, with or without food, at about the same time each day. Swallow the tablet whole. Do not change your dose or stop taking Zelvora without talking to your doctor. Most patients in the (fictional) studies saw less itching within 4 weeks.

turns.text: Yes, I take it once a day, same time. No, not really. No questions. Oh, my ankles have been a bit swollen this week. Probably the heat. Goodbye. Goodbye.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: I'm sorry to hear about the swollen ankles — I've passed that to the safety team as well. The Zelvora support line is open Monday to Friday, 9 am to 6 pm, if you need anything else. Thank you for your time, Maria — take care.
